candidate_relations.reason: The new lung infiltrates after ipilimumab–nivolumab are an immune-related adverse event, but this umbrella term omits the pulmonary organ diagnosis.
The infiltrates arose after eight immunotherapy courses and were attributed to checkpoint inhibition, so an idiopathic interstitial pneumonia assigns the wrong cause.
Grade 3 pneumonitis persisted despite two methylprednisolone pulses and high-dose prednisolone, directly supporting steroid-refractory checkpoint-inhibitor pneumonitis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: same pneumonitis with supported refractory state

candidate_relations.reason: Bilateral infiltrates developed on ipilimumab–nivolumab, failed antibiotics, and had negative bronchoscopic cultures, matching ICI-induced pneumonitis.
A broad autoimmune serologic panel was negative and no systemic autoimmune syndrome was identified beyond the treatment-related lung toxicity.
Bronchoscopy cultures were negative and the record contains no CMV PCR, inclusions, or viremia to establish CMV pneumonia.
Procalcitonin, sputum studies, and bronchoscopic cultures were negative, and broad antibiotics produced no improvement.
No herpetic cytopathic findings or HSV assay is reported, while the lymphocyte-rich lavage supports a noninfectious immune process.
